titleEn: From Wales to Finland, minority language speakers still face prejudice
titleZh: 从威尔士到芬兰，少数语言使用者仍然面临偏见
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: “How very rude to be speaking Welsh.”
paragraphs.zh: “说威尔士语真是太无礼了。”

paragraphs.en: That was the complaint a stranger directed at Patsy, a Welsh learner featured in my latest book, after overhearing her family speaking Welsh in a Cardiff cafe. She could hardly believe it: “But you’re in Wales. What are you talking about?”
paragraphs.zh: 这是一个陌生人在卡迪夫的一家咖啡馆里无意中听到她的家人说威尔士语后对帕齐的抱怨。帕齐是我最新一本书中的一位威尔士学习者。她几乎不敢相信：“但你在威尔士。你在说什么？”

paragraphs.en: Wales has come a long way since the days of the Welsh not, a wooden token often accompanied by corporal punishment that was used in some 19th-century schools to discourage children from speaking Welsh. The Welsh language is now more visible, more widely supported and more politically protected than at any point in history.
paragraphs.zh: 威尔士语“不”（Welsh not）是一种木制的象征，19世纪的一些学校曾用它来劝阻孩子们不要说威尔士语，但与此相比，威尔士已经走过了漫长的道路。威尔士语现在比历史上任何时候都更显眼，更广泛地得到支持，也更受政治保护。

paragraphs.en: But my ongoing research of Welsh-speaking families living in Cardiff suggests that while attitudes have improved dramatically, some linguistic prejudice still lingers beneath the surface. The pattern is not unique to Wales. I found similar experiences among Finland’s Swedish-speaking minority, where official recognition of the language has not always translated into acceptance in everyday life.
paragraphs.zh: 但我对居住在卡迪夫的讲威尔士语的家庭进行的持续研究表明，尽管态度有了显著改善，但一些语言偏见仍然在表面之下徘徊。这种模式并非威尔士独有。我在芬兰讲瑞典语的少数民族中发现了类似的经历，官方对瑞典语的承认并不总是转化为日常生活中的接受。

paragraphs.en: Several of the Welsh-speaking parents I interviewed had experienced negative attitudes towards Welsh when they were growing up in the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s. One father remembered being verbally abused for speaking Welsh in Cardiff as a child. Yet he was clear that things had changed.
paragraphs.zh: 我采访的几位讲威尔士语的父母在20世纪70、80和90年代的成长过程中，对威尔士语持负面态度。一位父亲记得小时候在卡迪夫因为讲威尔士语而受到辱骂。但他很清楚，情况已经发生了变化。

paragraphs.en: Other participants described being stereotyped or made to feel uncomfortable because they spoke Welsh. They felt that such prejudice was less obvious today, but could still appear in subtle ways, sometimes disguised as humour.
paragraphs.zh: 其他参与者描述说，他们因为讲威尔士语而被定型或感到不舒服，他们认为这种偏见今天不那么明显，但仍然可以以微妙的方式出现，有时伪装成幽默。

paragraphs.en: One Welsh-speaking teacher described becoming more aware of negative attitudes towards Welsh after moving from a Welsh-medium school to an English-medium one. The difference between generations was notable. Parents in my study could recall experiences of stereotyping, discrimination or prejudice. Their children had experienced very little of this.
paragraphs.zh: 一位说威尔士语的老师描述说，从威尔士语学校转到英语学校后，他越来越意识到人们对威尔士语的负面态度。代际差异很明显。我研究中的家长可以回忆起刻板印象、歧视或偏见的经历。他们的孩子几乎没有经历过这样的事情。

paragraphs.en: Younger participants had also grown up in an environment where Welsh was more visible and where there were more opportunities to use it outside the home. This meant that speaking Welsh could feel like an ordinary part of everyday life rather than something that marked them out.
paragraphs.zh: 年轻的参与者也是在威尔士语更常见的环境中长大的，在那里有更多的机会在家庭之外使用威尔士语。这意味着说威尔士语可以感觉像是日常生活的一部分，而不是让他们与众不同的东西。

paragraphs.en: A comparison with Finland
paragraphs.zh: 与芬兰比较

paragraphs.en: The experiences of the Welsh speakers became even more interesting when I compared them with those of Swedish speakers in Finland. Swedish was once the language of Finland’s political, economic and cultural elite. It remains one of the country’s two national languages alongside Finnish but is now spoken as a first language by only around 5% of the population. Like Welsh in Wales, it has a long history and a recognised place in public life. But speakers can still encounter negative attitudes.
paragraphs.zh: 当我把讲威尔士语的人的经历与在芬兰讲瑞典语的人的经历进行比较时，他们的经历变得更加有趣。瑞典语曾经是芬兰政治、经济和文化精英的语言。它仍然是芬兰的两种民族语言之一，与芬兰语并列，但现在只有大约5%的人口将其作为第一语言。就像威尔士的威尔士语一样，它有着悠久的历史，在公共生活中也有着公认的地位。2但演讲者仍然会遇到负面的态度。

paragraphs.en: One Swedish-speaking Finnish father told me that colleagues had expressed prejudice against Swedish speakers during lunch, unaware that he himself was one. He was particularly taken aback by their remarks, as he had regarded his new colleagues as educated and worldly.
paragraphs.zh: 一位会说瑞典语的芬兰父亲告诉我，同事们在午餐时对说瑞典语的人表达了偏见，而他并不知道自己也是瑞典人。他们的言论让他特别吃惊，因为他认为他的新同事受过教育，而且世故。

paragraphs.en: A Finnish mother remembered being a teenager when she and a friend were speaking Swedish on a train. Two adults left the carriage after hearing them, saying they did not want to sit near Swedish speakers. She only recognised the incident as discrimination much later. She also felt that this kind of public hostility had become less common. As in Wales, her children had not experienced the same kind of prejudice.
paragraphs.zh: 一位芬兰母亲回忆起她十几岁时和一个朋友在火车上讲瑞典语的情景。两个成年人听到他们的话后离开了车厢，说他们不想坐在讲瑞典语的人旁边。她很久以后才意识到这件事是歧视。她还觉得这种公开的敌意已经不那么常见了。和在威尔士一样，她的孩子没有经历过同样的偏见。

paragraphs.en: The incidents happened in different countries and involved different languages but the pattern was similar. In both Wales and Finland, older generations remembered more overt hostility. Younger people, meanwhile, appeared to be growing up with greater acceptance of the minority language.
paragraphs.zh: 这些事件发生在不同的国家，涉及不同的语言，但模式是相似的。在威尔士和芬兰，老一代人记得更公开的敌意。与此同时，年轻人似乎在更大程度上接受少数民族语言的情况下长大。

paragraphs.en: This suggests that official recognition and greater visibility can change the status of a language without necessarily eliminating the social attitudes that surround it.
paragraphs.zh: 这表明，官方承认和更大的知名度可以改变一种语言的地位，而不一定消除围绕它的社会态度。

paragraphs.en: Attitudes towards a language can influence whether families continue to pass it from one generation to the next. For minority languages, this is important because the process of parents passing a language on to their children is one of the main ways a language survives.
paragraphs.zh: 对一种语言的态度会影响到家庭是否继续将这种语言代代相传，对少数民族语言来说，这一点很重要，因为父母将一种语言传给子女的过程是一种语言得以生存的主要方式之一。

paragraphs.en: Positive attitudes alone are not enough. People also need opportunities to use the language in everyday life, and they need to feel that doing so is accepted. Children today are more likely to encounter Welsh in schools, public services, the media and cultural life. They may also see Welsh-speaking adults and peers using the language outside the home.
paragraphs.zh: 光有积极的态度是不够的。人们还需要在日常生活中使用威尔士语的机会，他们需要感到这样做是被接受的。今天的孩子更有可能在学校、公共服务、媒体和文化生活中接触到威尔士语。他们也可能看到讲威尔士语的成年人和同龄人在家庭之外使用威尔士语。

paragraphs.en: Research with children in Wales has found that those educated through the medium of Welsh tend to have more favourable attitudes towards the language than their English-medium peers. Exposure to Welsh-speaking people and communities can also help to build positive attitudes.
paragraphs.zh: 对威尔士儿童进行的研究发现，与以英语为媒介的同龄人相比，以威尔士语为媒介接受教育的儿童对威尔士语的态度往往更好。接触说威尔士语的人和社区也有助于建立积极的态度。

paragraphs.en: But there is still relatively little research into how Welsh speakers and non-Welsh speakers, perceive the language and its speakers.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，关于威尔士语使用者和非威尔士语使用者如何看待威尔士语及其使用者的研究仍然相对较少。

paragraphs.en: What has changed?
paragraphs.zh: 发生了什么变化？

paragraphs.en: Most of the Welsh-speaking parents in my research agreed things have changed. The kind of open hostility some experienced when they were young appears to be less common. Their children are growing up with greater opportunities to learn and use Welsh, and with more social and institutional support for doing so. But Patsy’s experience in that Cardiff cafe shows that greater visibility and official support do not automatically make prejudice disappear.
paragraphs.zh: 在我的研究中，大多数讲威尔士语的父母都同意情况已经发生了变化。一些人小时候所经历的那种公开的敌意似乎不那么常见了。他们的孩子在成长过程中有了更多的机会学习和使用威尔士语。但帕齐在卡迪夫咖啡馆的经历表明，更大的知名度和官方支持并不会自动造成偏见消失

paragraphs.en: The challenge for Welsh is therefore no longer simply to establish whether the language belongs in public life. It is to ensure that people feel able to use it there without being made to feel rude, difficult or out of place.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，威尔士语面临的挑战不再是简单地确定该语言是否属于公共生活，而是确保人们能够在公共生活中使用该语言，而不会感到粗鲁、困难或格格不入。

paragraphs.en: That means continuing to create opportunities to hear and use Welsh. But the experiences of Welsh speakers, and the similar stories from Finland, suggest that changing the status of a language is only part of the process. Changing the attitudes surrounding it can take much longer.
paragraphs.zh: 这意味着要继续创造听到和使用威尔士语的机会。但威尔士语使用者的经历以及芬兰的类似故事表明，改变一种语言的地位只是过程的一部分。改变人们对它的态度可能需要更长的时间。
